correctness.rationale: Detailed balance parametrizes the whole feasible set by unnormalized flows a,b,c and the two interior row caps. A disconnected chain has SLEM 1 and is immediately excluded from equality; in the Rayleigh step one may uniformly use the smallest generalized eigenvalue on the M-orthogonal complement of constants, including zero. For 0<t≤1, q=(r,1,−1,−r), r=1+√2, has Rayleigh quotient (a+c+2b)/(r²+t)≤2t/(r²+t)=γ*. Equality forces both interior caps tight and q to be an eigenvector, hence a=c=γ*r/(r−1) and b=t−a. At that feasible candidate, the even nonzero Laplacian eigenvalue e=a(1+1/t) exceeds γ*, and the odd characteristic polynomial at e is −2ab/t². Thus γ* is the smallest nonzero Laplacian eigenvalue, and the odd trace 2+a(1−1/t)≤2 controls the negative end of the transition spectrum. For t≥1, the endpoint antisymmetric unit vector gives a square-norm lower bound 1/(1+t) plus two squared deviations from a=c=t/(1+t). At those outer flows, saturation of the norm requires the odd block squared to have zero off-diagonal entry; the odd block's positive off-diagonal therefore forces its trace zero and b=t/2. Those weights give odd block square I/(1+t) and even nonstationary eigenvalue zero. The two branches agree at one, with derivatives −1/4 and −1/(4√2), and both interior holding rates change from zero to (t−1)/(2(t+1)). value.rationale: The interior-mass valley makes the standard harmonic walk infeasible and creates a natural active-constraint problem. The complete explicit design, certificate excluding asymmetric ties, and the first-derivative break at the switch provide an exact benchmark for discrete-time prescribed-mass path design beyond uniform stationarity. This is not a claim about arbitrary non-log-concave mass profiles.
